summary: Six commits on legion/LEGION-94 above the plan commit, rebased once onto main (bcdeff9f) because GitHub reported the pull request CONFLICTING: main's #1078 had already rewritten the inbox-ordering loop this plan's task 3 changed, so that commit was superseded and dropped. The Playwright config sets the suite's assertion timeout once (15 s); all 36 one- and two-second per-assertion budgets on cross-user and server-echo waits are gone and the two test names no longer promise 'within a second'; the approval test polls the API for the recorded review before navigating; the doc fixture ends in a paragraph so collaborative typing avoids the code block whose edit loss is LEGION-135; the workflow's failure-trace artifact carries the run attempt. One unplanned commit: four test files wrote debugging screenshots to hardcoded /tmp paths, which fail with EACCES on any shared host where another user left them; they now go to each test's own output dir. Full suite locally at the rebased head: see e2eSummaryLine.

fifthScenario.scenario: [iphone] e2e/doc.e2e.ts:317 tab round-trips keep one document connection, the typed text, and the Conversation scroll position
fifthScenario.classification: Local harness artefact; not a timing failure, not a product bug, and CI never had it. No test change.
fifthScenario.evidence: The trace of the one failure (unpacked from e2e/test-results at the time; frames read) shows a red 'Envoy unreachable: envoy listener unavailable: GET /v1/sessions returned 503' banner inside the Conversation composer. Cause: my pane exports ENVOY_URL=http://127.0.0.1:9020 (the real Envoy listener) and e2e/run-server.sh uses ${ENVOY_URL:-http://127.0.0.1:${FAKE_ENVOY_PORT}}, so the Go server asked the real listener, which answered 503 at that hour, instead of the fake Envoy; CI has no ENVOY_URL, so the fake Envoy answers /v1/sessions 200 and the banner never exists there. Mechanism in the trace: the agents query had never succeeded, so on the return to the Conversation tab TanStack Query refetched it and cleared the error while pending (banner gone at 161257 ms, the TODAY separator exposed), the refetch failed again (banner back at 161343 ms); each composer-height change is compensated by ReaderPosition so the anchored turn (Existing message 29) keeps its screen position in every frame — that compensation is what moved raw window.scrollY from 500 to 664 (the assertion reads raw scrollY). With the harness corrected the scenario passed 10/10 on iphone; with the banner forced (closed-port ENVOY_URL) it failed 10/10, so the banner is the deterministic cause and its intermittency in the first run was the real listener's intermittent 503.

deviations: Plan task 3 is not in the pull request: main's #1078 (7a1785815c1e) landed the same fix in a different form while this branch was in flight — the inbox-ordering test now creates its two clarifications through the API and awaits them before opening the Inbox, so there is no UI click for a reload to race. The rebase made this branch's task-3 commit empty and it was squashed away; the scenario is deterministic on main's version (see repeat runs).
One rebase, permitted because GitHub reported the pull request CONFLICTING; before/after fingerprints in `rebase` and in the PR comment.

Unplanned commit 871e0ea9: inbox.e2e.ts, agents.e2e.ts, ask-blocks.e2e.ts and polish.e2e.ts wrote debugging screenshots to fixed /tmp/*.png paths; on this shared box those files exist owned by another user, so the scenarios fail with EACCES on both projects (the only failures of the full-suite runs at fc35b96e — 196 passed, 2 failed — and at the rebased head fe3b9a9a — 202 passed, 8 failed, the six new ones from tests main added since the fork point). CI's /tmp is clean, so CI never saw it. Every such path now comes from testInfo.outputPath(), the per-test output dir the workflow uploads on failure (the two ask-blocks tests that lacked the testInfo fixture parameter gain it). Mechanical; the architect can hold the PR to the plan's commits by dropping this one.

Local toolchain: this pane's user has no Node 20+ (Playwright refuses Node 18) and mise's Go is not on the login-shell PATH, so the suite ran with an ephemeral Node 22.14.0 extracted under /tmp/l94-node and ~/.local/share/mise/installs/go/1.26.8/bin on PATH; nothing was installed on the box. Postgres: the existing dispatch-pg container from packages/envoy/scripts/dev-postgres.sh with a fresh database dispatch_l94 (createdb), DISPATCH_E2E_PORT=8794 and FAKE_ENVOY_PORT=9094 to avoid other agents' runs, ENVOY_URL and ENVOY_NATS_URL unset so run-server.sh targets the fake Envoy exactly as CI does.
trickyParts: run-server.sh inherits ENVOY_URL when the environment has one; a Legion pane always has one (the real listener). Any local run of this suite from a Legion pane must unset it or the Go server talks to production Envoy (reads only, for the doc/inbox/approval tests; the btw and message-agent tests would POST /v1/messages/send to it).

The negative control for the fifth scenario needed a guaranteed banner: pointing ENVOY_URL back at the real listener no longer reproduced it because the listener had recovered (answers /v1/sessions 200 now), so a closed port was used.
openQuestions: Observation for the architect, not filed: while Envoy is unreachable, every return to the Conversation tab makes the 'Envoy unreachable' banner disappear and reappear (the never-succeeded agents query clears its error while refetching). Cosmetic flicker; not in this issue's scope; decide whether it deserves a LEGION issue.

Observation: the tab round-trip scenario asserts raw window.scrollY, while the product deliberately adjusts scrollY to keep the reader's turn in place when content above it reflows. Deterministic in CI (no reflow there); left unchanged per the architect's instruction not to widen the scenario.
